s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory illness with systemic symptoms and neurological involvement
salient_findings: Cough, subjective fever, and shortness of breath
Right upper lobe infiltrate and diffuse crackles in the right lung base
Development of right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with an asymmetrically miotic right pupil
Leukocytosis and positive fungal antigen tests
key_facts: 81-year-old man with coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus
Initial treatment with azithromycin and levofloxacin for bronchitis
Symptoms progressed despite antibiotics
Vital signs: Temperature 38.6°C, Pulse 130 beats/min, Blood Pressure 114/61 mm Hg, Respiratory Rate 22 breaths/min, Oxygen Saturation 82%
Lung sounds were diminished in the right upper lobe, with diffuse crackles in the right lung base
Cardiac examination showed tachycardic irregularly irregular rhythm, systolic ejection murmur, and mild pitting edema
Leukocytosis: 15,000/mm³
Positive Blastomyces urine antigen and positive Histoplasmosis blood antigen
Negative results for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Cryptococcus, Legionella, and influenza
Bronchoscopy findings: Moderate clear secretions with erythematous and edematous bronchial mucosa
Bronchoalveolar lavage: Spherical broadly based budding yeast on Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver stain

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Blastomyces urine antigen and clinical presentation of progressive respiratory illness with systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Histoplasmosis blood antigen and clinical presentation of progressive respiratory illness with systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although antigen test was negative, it remains a consideration due to the patient's immunocompromised state and neurological involvement

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Given the patient's history of heart failure and chronic kidney disease, Aspergillosis is a plausible diagnosis, especially with the presence of leukocytosis and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's history of heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, along with the presence of leukocytosis and respiratory symptoms, makes Nocardiosis a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: Positive Blastomyces urine antigen and spherical broadly based budding yeast on Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver stain from bronchoalveolar lavage, which are characteristic findings for Blastomycosis

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Although Histoplasmosis blood antigen was positive, the presence of Blastomyces urine antigen and specific fungal morphology on Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver stain points more strongly towards Blastomycosis

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Negative antigen tests for Cryptococcus make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: No specific evidence for Aspergillosis, such as Aspergillus antigen or hyphae on microscopy, was provided

rejected.label: Nocardiosis
rejected.why: No evidence of Nocardia infection, such as positive cultures or characteristic Gram stain findings, was mentioned
